/* Read a whole file into a NUL-terminated buffer, or return NULL.
   The caller owns the buffer and frees it. */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

// The buffer grows by doubling; it starts one page big.
#define CHUNK 4096

char *read_file(const char *path) {
    FILE *fp = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (fp == NULL) {
        return NULL;
    }
    size_t cap = CHUNK;
    size_t len = 0;
    char *buf = malloc(cap);
    while (1) {
        if (len + 1 >= cap) {
            cap *= 2;
            char *grown = realloc(buf, cap);
            if (grown == NULL) {
                free(buf);
                fclose(fp);
                return NULL;
            }
            buf = grown;
        }
        size_t got = fread(buf + len, 1, cap - len - 1, fp);
        if (got == 0) {
            break; /* eof or error: either way, we are done */
        }
        len += got;
    }
    buf[len] = '\0';
    fclose(fp);
    return buf;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    if (argc < 2) {
        fprintf(stderr, "usage: %s <file>\n", argv[0]);
        return 1;
    }
    char *text = read_file(argv[1]);
    if (text == NULL) {
        perror("read_file");
        return 1;
    }
    printf("file is %zu bytes long\n", strlen(text));
    free(text);
    return 0;
}
